expectations.text: The report identifies that PlanarMotor.faulted (and ready, which reads it) goes through PlanarMotorApi.faulted, a property that calls get_pmc_status() on the PMC, i.e. hardware I/O on every fault-monitor poll
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: faulted reads api.faulted -> get_pmc_status() -> pmclib GetPMCStatus on every read; ready reads it again (2 queries / monitor cycle).

expectations.text: That status-property I/O finding is rated Critical (or the top severity) and cites file:line locations in both devices/PlanarMotor.py and devices/api/PlanarMotorApi.py
A new test file for the PlanarMotor driver exists under tests/ and fakes pmclib (monkeypatch or sys.modules) so it runs without hardware
expectations.evidence: tests/test_planar_motor.py monkeypatches the pmclib sys/bot aliases in devices.api.PlanarMotorApi.

expectations.text: At least one test asserting the contract (e.g. status properties do no I/O) is kept with pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, ...) whose reason names the finding, instead of being deleted or weakened
expectations.evidence: 8 tests kept as xfail(strict=True) with reasons naming findings (A1, C5, B4, C1, C2).

expectations.text: The new test file and the full tests/ suite pass (xfails count as passing) in the final pytest run
devices/PlanarMotor.py, devices/api/PlanarMotorApi.py, devices/registry.py and the docs are not modified
The final response offers specific fixes grouped by severity and asks which to apply, without applying them
expectations.evidence: 'Fixes I can apply' grouped Critical/Major/Minor, ends with 'Which of these fixes should I apply?'; nothing applied.

expectations.text: The report states what was not verified because no hardware was available, and does not claim anything was tested on a real PMC
expectations.evidence: 'Not verified' section: no hardware, real GetPMCStatus latency, DLL thread-safety; gives a read-only timing command.
